answer: Withdrawing stake burns a 9% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the vine fee is applied at the zephyr exit, the quartz audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. That is 15 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
